notes.title: Version 1.2.3: New Demo!
notes.content:
Last Friday I attended an Oslo Gamedev Meetup and some of the people there tried my game, and it quickly became obvious there were two big issues!

The first one was problematic, quite a few of the players actually skipped the intro sequence completely without really noticing, which meant they did not actually get to read the instructions!

The second one is that the demo version was old. Quite old, it was actually based on the version 1.1.0 from March this year, which means it was missing quite a few quality of life improvements, item descriptions, interactions and images as well. Plus also the fact the demo was quite short so one of the players actually found the back of the house in just a couple minutes and reached the end.

So this version 1.2.3 solves these three issues:
[list]
[*] The intro sequence is now skipped by pressing ESCape instead of SPACE or ENTER (but a text tells you if you bash the keyboard and nothing happens)
[*] The demo version has been updated to this same version 1.2.3
[*] The demo now allows you to enter the house (so you have access to the basement and ground floor), more than tripling the amount of things you can do in the game
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45293708/6aa3ed702eec19c86ef780eca95dc65a6ab90c5b.png[/img]

I hope you'll like the changes, and feel free to point out any issue you see!

notes.title: Version 1.2.2: We have Clafoutis!
notes.content:
This version 1.2.2 was not originally planned, but during the summer holidays, I observed family members playing the game and noted a few minor issues. Not all are resolved in this new version, but I’m committed to addressing them in future updates, as I dislike leaving bugs in my programs.

Additionally, the Atari ST demoscene community sparked a lively discussion about “clafoutis” - a French dessert traditionally made with cherries - thanks to the recently released game Galactic Panic.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45293708/2828f966518dee931eca80b1fcf9092ac0be9bad.jpg[/img]

This led to requests to incorporate clafoutis in Encounter. 

Fortunately, the game’s unused orchard with previously useless (yet tasty) apples provided the perfect opportunity: Players can now eat, chop, and use apples, potentially for gameplay purposes, such as solving an enigma. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45293708/fb2809a27372c4418818a4b21d6a7080fb59aeb6.png[/img]

Here’s the full list of changes:
[list]
[*]Shifted the achievement list to the left to prevent French achievements from corrupting the screen.
[*]Canceling item selection from a container now ignores the operation instead of displaying an error.
[*]Updated the incorrect container message to “This is not a usable container” from “That will not work.”
[*]Added the ability to eat, chop, and use apples.
[*]Inserted key press waits after certain description texts for better pacing.
[*]Corrected minor typos in description texts.
[*]Added description texts for the knife and dart gun.
[/list]

notes.title: Achievements in French.
notes.content:
The downside of developing on a machine set to one language is that you don’t always notice issues in others! 

This summer, while on vacation, I installed the game on my parents’ computer and realized the achievements were in English on Steam’s interface (but correctly in French in *Encounter*). 

This issue should now be fixed. 

Sorry for the inconvenience!

notes.title: Strategy tips for new adventurers
notes.content:
When I presented the game to people who had never played a classic adventure game before, it quickly became clear that they were unsure how to proceed. They would either wander aimlessly and get lost, collect every item they saw until their inventory was full, or fail to pick up items and forget where they had been.

To assist new players, I wrote [url=https://www.defence-force.org/index.php?page=games&game=encounter&type=help]this article[/url] , which covers topics like making a map, managing items, and more.

Hopefully, this will help you all!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45293708/c68320bc99ed7ae196183b7d8330ab3e8fba7a7e.png[/img]

notes.title: Final version!
notes.content: [p]We are reaching the end of the project!  [/p][p][/p][p]Encounter was released in December 2024, and since then, there has been a steady stream of improvements and tweaks. However, I've reached the point where the disk is completely full, and so is the game's memory.  [/p][p][/p][p]For those who haven't followed the project, this is not a typical PC game. It's a game running on a 1984 computer called the Oric, with a 1 MHz 6502 processor, 64 kilobytes of memory, and 380 kilobytes of storage on a 3" floppy disk, all running in an emulator called Oricutron. As a result, the game cannot expand indefinitely: there are very real physical limits.  [/p][p][/p][p]For this final version (though I may release a couple more updates if bugs are found, this is considered "feature complete" in terms of content), I've added a few images:  [/p][p][/p][p]Now, when investigating the well, you get a proper picture:  [/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45293708/ccdff83424f503b3a175b2d4a8ecfc64a8ffe22b.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]You also get an image when investigating the trash cans in the alley:  [/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45293708/7deb2bc2cfcdd60c5f0e610953e9b1da8430c6b8.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]And in the guest room of the mansion, you can find a well-worn first edition of Frank Herbert's Dune:  [/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45293708/4a7c0a3153f25fb7e4dcf9673801b8a7e33382ab.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]That's it! If you've been waiting for the final version of the game before playing, this is the one!  [/p][p][/p][p]Thanks to everyone who supported the project. I'm now going to take a break and may return with more games once my batteries are recharged. :)[/p]

notes.title: Version 1.2: Monkey King!
notes.content:
This version 1.2.0 finally brings in a playable Monkey King minigame!

If you played the game before, you may have found a handheld device in one of the rooms, but unfortunately it was not playable because it was out of batteries.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45293708/399e7e289bd640a3eb075758dcfc9d2ea1525171.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45293708/0379728e902e399539dd0d2cacb7422639b7fb05.png[/img]

Some assembly is required, but you'll be rewarded with a fully playable Monkey King game, complete with normal and fast modes, and saved scores (and your best score for the session will be added to the final in-game Encounter score).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45293708/21156780111816bd59e4180c9344ab2f790bbbf8.png[/img]

This version 1.2.0 will most likely be the last big update: If I can fit a few more images on the disk I may push a couple minor versions, possibly the QR Code generator will be inserted so games can be shared on the Defence Force website on some online leaderboard, but that's about it.

If you bought the game, thank you, and I really hope you enjoyed it despite all the limitations coming with making a game fit in less than 400 KB on disk!

notes.title: Version 1.1.2: Back to BASIC!
notes.content:
As you can see, the development of the game is [b]not yet finished[/b]!

I only had a few bytes remaining on disk, so many of the things I wanted to add were unfortunately impossible to do... but then I remembered that my storage system only used 17 sectors per track while the hardware would work just fine with 18 sectors... which brings us an addition 256 bytes for each track on the floppy, and since we have 42 tracks on each side, that adds 256x42x2 = 21504 bytes for new data.

This format change has been tested on a real Oric Atmos on LOCI, Cumulus and Cumana Reborn, but if you experience some issues on your machine, then please get in touch so we can solve that!

There will hopefully be [b]new versions with additional content[/b], but in this new version the only change is that you will now be able to find an Oric 1 computer in the games room, and when trying to use it the game will ask you if you are ok to abort the game session. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45293708/177d65bec3954e136eeefce0d464e0b7430bd96f.png[/img]

If you answer Y (yes) the game will reset the machine and you will end up on the Oric BASIC prompt.

Technically the Oric 1 would have been using the ROM 1.0, but the ROM 1.1 is much nicer to use (fewer bugs), so if you want to play with BASIC programming feel free to try!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45293708/b3bd7235a31a380c5953ad7a70da466e39129ec6.png[/img]

If you have never programmed in BASIC, you can find a PDF copy of the [url=https://library.defence-force.org/books/content/oric1manual.pdf]Oric 1[/url] or [url=https://library.defence-force.org/books/content/manual_atmos.pdf]Oric Atmos[/url] manual in the Oric Library


Here is the detailed list of changes:
[list]
[*]First version of the game using 18 sectors per track instead of 17, this adds 21 KB of storage on disk and should not impact compatibility.
[*]Added an Oric 1 computer in the games room, can be used to access the BASIC prompt from the game
[*]Changed the default configuration of the emulator to use software rendering instead of OpenGL (except for the full crt emulation mode)
[*]Trying to take some of the items will now ask if you are kleptomaniac instead of just printing "can't do this"
[/list]

notes.content:

notes.title: Version 1.1.0: Joystick support, Steam Deck!
notes.content:
This is a relatively big update, the game itself has not changed but a new alternative control scheme has been added which should make it easier to play (assuming you have a compatible controller), in addition, the new version of Oricutron should help with some of the keyboard issues and the ugly status bar is finally gone!

The game has been tested on Steam Deck and is working nicely, the documentation will have to be updated to reflect the changes but before that happens I need a few of you to actually try the game on Steam Deck and report if it works well for you!

The way it works is simple (assuming you are using the layout I defined):
- Use any of the directional controls (dpad, analog sticks, touch pads) to move in the four directions
- Use the diagonals to move up and down (on stairs, ladders and ropes)
- Pressing the A button shows a selection menu for the commands and items and you just need to use the directional controls to move around and A again to select the option you want.

And that's about it really!

I would really appreciate if any issue/regression is reported so I can address them, and if you liked the game, please give a review on the main page, it's always good for the motivation. 

Thanks in advance!

1.1.0
- Modified the settings menu to be more reactive and have the joystick options at the bottom
- Support for joystick interfaces (IJK, Pase, Opel, Dk'Tronic)
- New control scheme using four direction joysticks and single button selection usable on both Oric and Steam Deck devices
- Updated Oricutron to a more recent version with better controllers handling, removal of the status bar, immersive mode, etc...

You can see how this new control scheme work on this video (in English only)

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EDrwQv9KYbY

notes.title: Version 1.0.5
notes.content:
The only significant change in this version is that the parser will no longer accept additional keywords if they are not relevant to the command.

For example, instructions like PAUSE or QUIT don't take any parameters, but previously, the game would not complain if you tried to PAUSE ROPE or QUIT TREE. The additional ROPE or TREE words were simply ignored.

Similarly, USE or READ only require a single item name after them. So, USE ROPE TREE would work but would be the same as USE ROPE. Now, if you try that, the input will simply be refused.

Hopefully, this will help remove some confusion!

notes.title: Launch day!
notes.content:
This is [b]launch day[/b]! A day which is both exciting and full of unknowns!

After working on this game for so long, it feels like a scary milestone, but hey, not much we can do at this point. Players will hopefully enjoy the game, and for those who don't, that's okay because this is not a game for everybody!

No change log in this message. Let's just say that the current version would not have been as good without the active participation of a few individuals (known as Dom, Lukas, Phreak, Retroric, and Symoon) who have been reporting numerous issues [i]("If you do this and that after having done that, then this happens, is that on purpose?")[/i], typographical and grammatical errors, and making suggestions regarding colors, the position of things on screen, etc.

So yes, I (Mickaël) created most of the game as it is now, but without their contribution (as well as Per, who composed the music for the game and trailer), it would have been a much less enjoyable piece of software.

I'm sure some people will find some issues, and there will be new versions to address these, but hopefully, the game is in a state solid enough to be enjoyable as it is!

Personally, I'm interested in knowing what the modern Steam PC audience will think of this game. In a world where most games now require SSDs and dozens or hundreds of gigabytes of storage, fast CPUs, and dedicated GPUs, releasing a game that limits itself to what you can achieve with a 1 MHz 8-bit processor, 64 KB of memory, and 360 KB of disk storage is probably kind of crazy... but hey, it was an interesting experience anyway.

No matter what you think of the game (good or bad), please leave a review so I have some interesting stuff to read!

[b]Merry Christmas, everybody![/b]

notes.title: Encounter 0.9.1
notes.content:
The silence in the last two weeks did not mean the project was abandoned. On the contrary, numerous bugs have been fixed, some interactions have been added pretty much all over the place, and the French version is almost complete.

Obviously you are reading the English version of the text, so you don't really care about the French version, but since the plan is to launch with both languages simultaneously, it was quite important that the French version got some love as well.

So anyway, the game is on track for the launch on the 20th, so far so good!

Here is the complete patch notes for version 0.9.1
[list]
[*] French localization is now almost complete, for both the texts and images ("digicode message", "recipes", "tombstone" and saved" image at the end), kerning and comic bubbles placements have been adapted to the different lengths
[*] Added quite a few item descriptions and interactions.
[*] Fixed a bunch of things that can be opened and closed so the game reports they are already open or closed instead of just doing a weird refresh of the screen.
[*] Fixed an audio glitch when trying to play musics with music disabled caused by the channel mixer being modified anyway.
[*] Fixed some typos, improved the display of error messages so they are on purple background with the large font instead of the small red text.
[*] Fixed the pipe character in the font to be a ô in French because I use the word "Plutôt" somewhere and it was showing as a vertical arrow.
[*] Fixed the set item location command to make sure it drops the contained item if a non empty container is dropped (or thrown).
[*] If the dove fly away, the chirping sound stops in the wooded avenue
[*] Inspecting the acid shows the description image again
[*] Inspecting the alarm panel now informs there is a hole for a key
[*] Inspecting the black tape now suggests it's possible to remove it
[*] Inspecting the bomb now shows some comment instead of "nothing special"
[*] Inspecting the book shows the usual message and then goes on reading it. (and same thing with the recipes).
[*] Inspecting the girl now tells the player that she is unharmed and quite relieved.
[*] Inspecting the note now makes you read it instead of saying "nothing special".
[*] Inspecting the window up stairs is now possible.
[*] It should not be possible anymore to use the hose if it's already in use, instead an error message is displayed saying it's already installed.
[*] It's now possible to just press enter if we don't have a valid container, before you would get stuck there until you entered something invalid.
[*] Looking at the front entrance now suggest to look for a back entrance.
[*] Made sure that using the wrong container shows a message telling the user they should use something more adapted.
[*] Modified the gun powder so it can be transported in any adequate (for powder) container.
[*] Modified the pit message to make it clear that without a rope or ladder you are not going to be able to go up again.
[*] Modified the script to code to ensure that we can't create a bomb in a plastic bag or cardboard box.
[*] Moved the "hose" from the zen garden to the fish pond
[*] Moved the "fishing net" to the tennis court instead of the fishing pond and renamed it to just a "net"
[*] Opening and closing the parts of the car will now properly report that they are already opened or closed.
[*] Removed the complicated pause logic with double achievement, simpler, and more memory available, the second achievement is now hooked to closing the fridge
[*] Removed the Microdisc/Jasmin achievements and instead hooked them to the invoice and tombstone.
[*] Replaced the "Don't be ridiculous" by "That will not work"
[*] Updated the scores to include information about if a score was pre-made or made by an actual player.
[*] Using the matches with petrol or gunpowder around will result in an explosion: Kid: Don't play with matches!
[*] When building the fuse the petrol and the roll now vanish forever, that was just confusing.
[/list]

notes.title: Achievements!
notes.content:
It's difficult for an [b]emulated [/b]game to access things like the Steam API, but I did [b]promise [/b]that I would try my best to get the in-game achievements onto Steam if I could find a way!

The method I used is kind of [b]wonky[/b], but it works.

Basically the game launcher (I know, everybody hates them) tracks [b]changes[/b] done to the virtual [b]floppy [/b]containing the game data, and when it changes it loads the modified content which happens to contain the player score and any unlocked achievements.

After that it's just a matter of matching these with the Steam achievements and [b]trigger [/b]them.

Unfortunately there are 48 achievements, and it takes a [b]lot of time[/b] to create them and then test them, but here is what the [strike]24 [/strike] 25 first achievements look like!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45293708/d9587f966ad8d5c3ec5dbf19ba78b7a795a93e58.png[/img]

None of these achievements are hidden, but I kind of [b]obfuscated [/b]what their represent to avoid making it too easy to know what they actually represent.

[i](If too many people struggle to unlock some of them I will consider making these more obvious)[/i]

Another thing to keep in mind is that the game only saves the achievements at the end of a [b]play session[/b], so they will not trigger immediately, this will only happen when you reach the credits - which happens as soon as your reach an ending condition such as victory or one of the many game over events -

Hopefully that's an acceptable trade-off, there's so much magic I can do with 64KB of RAM!

notes.title: Encounter 0.9.0
notes.content:
This version comes with a new version of the game which has quite a few changes, as well as a first version of the Steam Cloud Saves (right now only saves the configuration, but the next version will remember the scores and hopefully the achievements so they don't get lost if a new version of the game is published.

Additionally both the French and English versions of the game are in the downloaded package, and the launcher let you launch whichever version you wish.

0.9.0:
- The clock is now stopped during a game over sequence
- The "rough map" is now a "rough plan" to not conflict with the map of the uk in the library
- Modified CTRL+DELETE so it erases the input word by word.
- When a wrong input is detected, the input field briefly turns red
- The "set of keys" was renamed "a small key", when inspected says it's for the alarm system, and trying to use it on the front door says it does not fit
- Trying to open the alarm panel now shows that the panel is locked instead of the door being locked
- When the black tape is removed, the window on the outside now properly appeared cleared

One month to go, hopefully the Steam achievements are doable as well!

notes.title: Encounter 0.8.9
notes.content:
Here is a list of changes:

The game has been updated to version 0.8.9 with the following changes:
- The chemistry recipes now spawn in the library items instead of the inventory
- The delays when moving with the arrows and when going in the wrong direction have been reduced
- The keyboard buffer is flushed when the prompt is displayed to avoid some confusing inputs
- The ladder is now visible in the orchard
- Added an attempt at scrolling the inventory using SHIFT+UP/SHIFT+DOWN
- Added a primitive input validation on the individual words to see if they are at least valid words (does not check if their presence is legal or not though)

In addition, this version now has a proper launcher that allows settings parameters such as full screen or windowed mode, English or French language, and the selection of render mode (normal, scanline, crt)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45293708/663e1c208537da4ae0785e8d91eb62cc7ea8a882.png[/img]

This launcher is still very much work in progress, so expect changes in the following weeks!
